newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANDELSBANKEN LOOKS FOR BIG ESTONIA SHARE.
newsitem.headline: HANDELSBANKEN LOOKS FOR BIG ESTONIA SHARE.

text.p: Sweden's Handelsbanken said it was seeking to be a significant player on the Estonian market after buying Estonian broker and corporate finance company Aktoris.
"Our intention is to be an significant player in the local market here," Bo Kragh, head of Handelsbanken's Tallinn office, told a news conference.
The purchase will allow Aktoris as the 100 percent locally registered corporate finance group to sell the services of its large Swedish investor.
"The aim is to be able to provide more efficient products in in the Estonian investment sector," said Auli Kumpulainen, managing director of Aktoris.
"Large Estonian companies will be able to use Svenska Handelsbanken services in Stockholm, Helsinki and in...London, Paris and other offices," she added.
Aktoris sees having one of Scandinavia's largest banks as one of the key ways to increase market share and foreign invesment in Estonia.

"In order to increase market share in Estonia ... it requires credibility when it comes to foreign investors and that credibility is very much achieved by having Hansdelsbanken as a share holder," said Kumpilainen.
But Aktoris was aware that there are problems with the size of the Estonian market for foreign investors.
"Estonia is a difficult market," Kumpulainen said.
She said that foreign firms do not usually want to get more than 10 percent of a company but have a minimum they can invest of some one million dollars.
However, in many cases in Estonia this sum is already more than 10 percent of the company's shares.
"Hopefully because of the booming secondary (equities market) the value of the companies will increase and it is easier to sell larger companies," she added.
